facts.text: The demand for a state of Marathi speaking people led to the 'Samyukta Maharashtra Movement' from 1946 onwards.
facts.quote: In Maharashtra also the demand for state of Marathi speaking people led to 'Samyukta Maharashtra Movement' from 1946 onwards.

facts.text: On 1 May 1960 the state of Maharashtra came to be formed.
facts.quote: finally on 1 May 1960 the state of Maharashtra came to be formed.

facts.text: From the beginning of the 20th century many scholars expressed thoughts on unification of Marathi speaking people.
facts.quote: From the beginning of 20th century, many scholars had begun to express the thoughts on unification of Marathi speaking people.

facts.text: In 1911 the British Government had to suspend the partition of Bengal; on this background N.C.Kelkar wrote that the entire Marathi speaking population should be under one dominion.
facts.quote: In 1911, the British Government had to suspend the partition of Bengal. On this background, N.C.Kelkar wrote that 'the entire Marathi speaking population should be under one dominion'.

facts.text: In 1915 Lokmanya Tilak demanded the reconstruction of a state based on language.
facts.quote: In 1915, Lokmanya Tilak had demanded the reconstruction of a state based on language.

facts.text: On 12 May 1946, an important resolution about Samyukta Maharashtra was passed in the Sahitya Sammelan at Belgaon.
facts.quote: On 12 May 1946, in the Sahitya Sammelan at Belgaon, an important resolution regarding Samyukta Maharashtra was passed.

facts.text: On 28 July the 'Maharashtra Ekikaran Parishad' was called at Mumbai, with Shankarrao Dev as its president.
facts.quote: On 28 July, 'Maharashtra Ekikaran Parishad' was called at Mumbai. Shankarrao Dev was its president.

facts.text: The Parishad resolved that all Marathi speaking regions, including those of Mumbai, Central provinces, Marathwada and Gomantak, should be in one state.
facts.quote: It passed a resolution that all Marathi speaking regions should be included in one state. This should also include Marathi speaking regions of Mumbai, Central provinces as well as Marathwada and Gomantak.

facts.text: On 17 June 1948 Dr. Rajendra Prasad, President of the Constituent Assembly, established the 'Dar Commission' under Justice S.K.Dar for forming linguistic provinces.
facts.quote: On 17 June 1948, Dr. Rajendra Prasad, the President of Constituent Assembly established the 'Dar Commission' under the chairmanship of Justice S.K.Dar, for forming linguistic provinces.

facts.text: On 10 December 1948 the report of the Dar Commission was published, but the issue remained unsolved.
facts.quote: On 10 December 1948, the report of Dar Commission was published but the issue remained unsolved.

facts.text: On 29 December 1948 the Congress appointed a committee of Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel and Pattabhisitaramayya, known by their initials as the 'JVP Committee'.
facts.quote: the Congress appointed a committee on 29 December 1948. It included Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel and Pattabhisitaramayya. It is known by the initials of these members as 'JVP Committee'.

facts.text: The JVP report accepted linguistic states in principle but said the time was not proper; there was severe response in Maharashtra and Senapati Bapat organised rallies.
facts.quote: The report suggested that Congress accepts the concept of linguistic state in principle but the time was not proper for it. Severe response was seen throughout Maharashtra against this report. During that time Senapati Bapat organised rallies for awakening of people.

facts.text: Acharya Atre got the proposal of Samyukta Maharashtra with Mumbai passed in the Mumbai Municipal Corporation by 50 against 35 votes.
facts.quote: Acharya Atre got passed the proposal of Samyukta Maharashtra with Mumbai in the Mumbai Municipal Corporation. It got passed by 50 against 35 votes.

facts.text: On 29 December 1953 the Government of India appointed a 'Commission for Reconstruction of States' under Justice Fazal Ali.
facts.quote: Government of India appointed a 'Commission for Reconstruction of States' on 29 December 1953, under the Chairmanship of Justice Fazal Ali.

facts.text: On 10 October 1955 the commission presented its proposal, which advocated creation of a bilingual Mumbai State.
facts.quote: This commission presented their proposal on 10 October 1955. This proposal advocated for creation of bilingual Mumbai State.

facts.text: The Nagpur Pact was signed in 1953 so that Marathi people of all regions would resolve to make one state; Samyukta Maharashtra was to include Western Maharashtra, Vidarbha and Marathwada.
facts.quote: Marathi people of all regions should resolve to make one state was the purpose of signing the Nagpur Pact in 1953. According to this pact, Samyukta Maharashtra was formed including Western Maharashtra and Vidarbha along with Marathwada.

facts.text: In 1956, by an amendment of the Constitution, Article 371 (2) was included.
facts.quote: In 1956, as per the ammendment of the Constitution, Article 371 (2) was included in it.

facts.text: The Nagpur Pact gave assurances such as fair finance for development, finance for technical and vocational education, state jobs by population, and an Assembly Session in Nagpur once a year.
facts.quote: According to the Nagpur Pact assurance was given regarding equitable financial provision for developmental work, ample finance for technical and vocational education, provision of state government services in particular regions in accordance with the population and Assembly Session once in a year should be held in Nagpur etc.

facts.text: At a huge meeting on Kamgar Maidan in Mumbai, Shankarrao Dev said they would oppose the separation of Mumbai from Maharashtra up to their last breath.
facts.quote: A huge meeting was held on Kamgar Maidan in Mumbai. At that time Shankarrao Dev said, 'We will oppose the seperation of Mumbai from Maharashtra upto our last breath'.

facts.text: Women like Sumatibai Gore, Ismat Chugtai, Durga Bhagwat, Tara Reddi, Charusheela Gupte, Kamalatai More and Sultana Johari took part in the agitation.
facts.quote: Sumatibai Gore, Ismat Chugtai, Durga Bhagwat, Tara Reddi, Charusheela Gupte, Kamalatai More, Sultana Johari and many such women took part in the agitation.

facts.text: On 7 November 1955 there was a meeting of labours presided over by Comrade Shripad Amrut Dange, where S.M.Joshi proposed Samyukta Maharashtra with Mumbai and Vidarbha.
facts.quote: On 7 November 1955, there was meeting of labours. ... Comrade Shripad Amrut Dange presided over it. Here S.M.Joshi proposed a resolution that Samyukta Maharashtra, with Mumbai and Vidarbha, should be created.

facts.text: A grand march led by Senapati Bapat was taken to the Vidhan Sabha when Morarji Desai was Chief Minister; the police used lathi charge and tear gas.
facts.quote: A grand march led by Senapati Bapat was taken to Vidhan Sabha. Morarji Desai was the Chief Minister at that time. The government declared a ban. The police started lathi charge and used tear gas.

facts.text: That evening an open meeting of around 50 thousand people was held on Kamgar Maidan, and Comrade Dange guided the people.
facts.quote: On that evening an open meeting was conducted on Kamgar Maidan with a mob of around 50 thousand. Comrade Dange guided the people.

facts.text: On 21 November 1955 a decision of a one day token strike was taken.
facts.quote: on 21 November 1955 decision of one day token strike was taken.

facts.text: On 6 February 1956 a meeting was held under the Chairmanship of Keshavrao Jedhe at Tilak Smarak Mandir in Pune to establish the Samyukta Maharashtra Samiti.
facts.quote: On 6 February 1956, a meeting was conducted under the Chairmanship of Keshavrao Jedhe at Tilak Smarak Mandir in Pune.

facts.text: The Samiti's Executive Council: Comrade Shripad Amrut Dange President, Dr. T.R.Naravane Vice President and S.M.Joshi General Secretary.
facts.quote: Comrade Shripad Amrut Dange as the President. Dr.T.R.Naravane as Vice President and S.M.Joshi as General Secretary were selected.

facts.text: G.T.Madkholkar, Acharya P.K.Atre, Madhu Dandavate, Prabodhankar Keshav Thackeray and Y.K. Souni played an important role in establishing the Samiti.
facts.quote: G.T.Madkholkar, Acharya P.K.Atre, Madhu Dandavate, Prabodhankar Keshav Thackeray, Y.K. Souni played important role in establishing the Samiti.

facts.text: Senapati Bapat, Krantisinh Nana Patil, Lalji Pendse and Ahilyabai Rangnekar spread the movement to rural parts of Maharashtra.
facts.quote: At the same time Senapati Bapat, Krantisinh Nana Patil, Lalji Pendse, Ahilyabai Rangnekar contributed immensely to the Samyukta Maharashtra movement. They spread the movement to rural parts of Maharashtra.

facts.text: When it was clear Mumbai would not be included, 106 people became martyrs in the firing opened by the State Government.
facts.quote: When it was clear that Mumbai will not be included in Maharashtra, at that time there arouse a huge public agitation. In this movement 106 people became martyrs in the firing opened by the State Government.

facts.text: In memory of the 106 martyrs, the 'Hutatma Smarak' was erected in Mumbai near Flora Fountain.
facts.quote: In memory of the 106 sons of Maharashtra who became martyr for formation of Samyukta Maharashtra, the 'Hutatma Smarak' was erected in Mumbai near Flora Fountain.

facts.text: On 1 November 1956 the Bilingual Mumbai State came into existence.
facts.quote: On 1 November 1956, Bilingual Mumbai State came into existence.

facts.text: In 1957 Loksabha, Vidhan Sabha and Mumbai Municipal Corporation elections were held; the Samyukta Maharashtra Samiti got grand success.
facts.quote: Later in 1957, Loksabha, Vidhan Sabha and Mumbai Municipal Corporation elections were held. Samyukta Maharashtra Samiti got grand success. These results made it clear that the voters were against bilingual state and in favour of Samyukta Maharashtra.

facts.text: Newspapers like Prabodhan, Kesari, Sakal, Navakal, Navyug and Prabhat worked for awakening of the people.
facts.quote: In this movement the role of newspapers was important. Prabodhan, Kesari, Sakal, Navakal, Navyug, Prabhat many such newspapers worked for awakening of the people.

facts.text: Acharya Atre started the 'Maratha' newspaper, which played an important role in the movement.
facts.quote: Acharya Atre started the 'Maratha' newspaper which played an important role in Samyukta Maharashtra Movement.

facts.text: Balasaheb Thackeray took up the pen name 'Mavla' and drew caricatures to make the movement comprehensive.
facts.quote: Balasaheb Thackeray took up the pen name 'Mavla' and drew caricatures to make the movement comprehensive.

facts.text: Lokshahir Annabhau Sathe, Shahir Amar Sheikh and Shahir D.N.Gavankar aroused public awakening through their writings.
facts.quote: Lokshahir Annabhau Sathe, Shahir Amar Sheikh and Shahir D.N.Gavankar through their writings aroused public awakening on a large scale.

facts.text: Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru was to unveil the statue of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj on horse on Pratapgad on 30 November 1957; the Samiti made a huge demonstration under Bhai Madhavrao Bagal.
facts.quote: The unveiling of statue of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj mounted on horse on Pratapgad was to be done at the hands of Prime Minister Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru on 30 November 1957. At that time Samyukta Maharashtra Samiti decided to make huge demonstration under the leadership of Bhai Madhavrao Bagal.

facts.text: S.M.Joshi, N.G.Gore, Jayantrao Tilak, P.K.Atre and Uddhavrao Patil were present; severe demonstrations were made at Pasarni Ghat and Poladpur.
facts.quote: Leaders like S.M.Joshi, N.G.Gore, Jayantrao Tilak, P.K.Atre, Uddhavrao Patil were present. Severe demonstrations were made at Pasarni Ghat and Poladpur.

facts.text: Indira Gandhi, President of Congress, supported the Samyukta Maharashtra movement.
facts.quote: At this instance, Indira Gandhi , President of Congress supported the Samyukta Maharashtra movement.

facts.text: The Central Government consented to two linguistic states, Maharashtra and Gujarat; in April 1960 Parliament passed the Mumbai Reorganisation Act.
facts.quote: The Central Government consented the two linguistic states- Maharashtra and Gujarat. In April 1960, the Parliament passed the Mumbai Reorganisation Act.

facts.text: At the dawn of 1 May 1960, at a special ceremony at Raj Bhavan on Labour Day, Pandit Nehru officially announced the formation of Maharashtra State.
facts.quote: At the dawn of 1 May 1960, in the special ceremony at Raj Bhavan, on occasion of Labour Day, Pandit Nehru officially announced the formation of Maharashtra State.

facts.text: Yashwantrao Chavan accepted the responsibility as the first Chief Minister of Maharashtra.
facts.quote: Yashwantrao Chavan accepted the responsibility as first Chief Minister of Maharashtra.
